findings.title: Proof coverage falsely promises identical semantics across separate interpreters
findings.description: Lines 9-13 claim that rule properties are enforced identically because the same bytecode runs everywhere and nothing can drift. The owner repository actually has separate Z3 semantics, a TypeScript bytecode engine, and a Rust Solana interpreter. Its current security register confirms a concrete authorization-relevant divergence: an omitted field named constructor can resolve to Object.prototype.constructor in the TypeScript engine but to null in Rust and the proof model. A rule such as delete: @data.constructor != null can consequently admit an attacker offchain despite being analyzed under different semantics. Sharing a bytecode wire format does not establish identical interpretation.
findings.recommendation: Remove the categorical parity guarantee. State that separate interpreters consume the same bytecode and that parity depends on conformance testing. Fix own-property field access, reject hazardous field names until fixed, and maintain differential tests across proof, TypeScript, and Rust semantics.
